Creatures, including allies and the caster when actually in the sphere, make CON: failure takes the shared 8d8 thunder; success takes half, rounded down. Each eligible object/section receives the shared 8d8 as one thunder packet against its actual material defenses and durability, without a save. No separate object-bonus die is added.

For each actual structural whole, select one contiguous exposed section wholly within the sphere, bounded by a five-foot cube, containing the reachable point nearest the center. Stable neutral geometry resolves equal choices before rolling; naming each brick or panel separately does not multiply one building's packets. An independently profiled freestanding structure or object remains genuinely distinct. Hidden boundaries are Director records, not information revealed by casting.

NEW a selected section is weak if its already established structural record marks it unstable/weak with a finite failure profile, or it is ordinary nonmagical wood, packed earth or crumbling masonry no more than one foot thick and already at or below half of its actual structural maximum HP before this blast. Missing durability is not treated as zero or automatically weak; establish the real object's finite profile before committing a spell that depends on it. Do not retrospectively invent damage or a weak support to reward a cast. Resolve thunder damage first. Any selected section actually reduced to structural zero fails normally. In addition, a prequalified weak section suffering positive post-defense thunder from this spell collapses even if its numeric HP would otherwise remain positive. Mark its structural integrity failed/zero without treating the extra loss as another damage packet or a resource-generating DamageDealt amount. Immunity preventing all its thunder means this extra collapse clause has no trigger.

After the original blast finishes, resolve real unsupported material and body falls. An existing finite structure/hazard profile controls the actual failure footprint, connected supports, height, escape and damage; a large cascade must be supported by that preexisting profile, not generated by recursively treating all newly exposed architecture as a new spell target. NEW fallback for a local weak section without a separate debris attack: its real falling material creates at most one debris event in that section's horizontal footprint plus five feet, and only up to twenty vertical feet below it.
